label: Model forecast
method: CDIP MOP nearshore wave model (ECMWF and WW3 forced, blended and bias-corrected at the buoys), then a random-wave shoaling and breaking model (Battjes–Janssen) from the model's 10 m point to the beach, using each swell's own period and direction. Wind: ECMWF IFS via Open-Meteo. Tide: NOAA La Jolla 9410230.
credits: CDIP / Scripps Institution of Oceanography, funded by USACE and California State Parks; MOP model: O'Reilly et al. (2016), Coastal Engineering 116
Wind: Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0), ECMWF IFS open data (CC BY 4.0)
Surf Zone Forecast, forecaster notes and alerts: National Weather Service San Diego

verification.what: Swell model (wave height offshore, not surf height) vs the CDIP buoys
verification.testPeriod: 2025-04-01 to 2026-11-26 (held out; never used for tuning)
beats: plain shoaling without island sheltering (RMSE ~1 m)
verification.notVerified: Small-day surf height (under about 6 ft) against people's observations, and the rating: no observations yet. Treat them as model estimates.
verification.scale: On small days our surf heights run about 20% above NWS surf forecasts; the Scripps Pier wave sensor (wave height just outside the surf zone) supports ours.
verification.observed: Breaking surf height, big days: 56 lifeguard and official high-surf reports (NWS storm reports, 2016–2026) matched our heights (median ratio 0.99; we reached at least 80% of the reported size on 93%). Small days: our heights track the Scripps Pier wave sensor (CDIP 073) closely over 1,538 small mornings (rank correlation 0.94). Small-day face heights are not yet checked against people's observations.
verification.leadNote: Scores are short-lead. Skill by forecast day is being collected.
verification.wind: Wind model chosen against the Scripps Pier anemometer (NOAA LJPC1): over 2026 mornings it got the wind type (glassy, offshore, cross or onshore) right about two times in three, with a typical speed error of 2.6 kt. Wind at other breaks is not checked.

periods.name: This Afternoon Through Saturday
periods.surf: 3 to 5 feet today increasing to 4 to 7 feet with local sets to 8 feet Saturday

paragraphs: High tide peaks this morning at 10 AM around 7.57-7.7 ft MLLW. High tides will continue to decrease through the weekend, with high tide around 7 ft MLLW Saturday, falling below 7 ft on Sunday. Forecast tides have been adjusted 1.01 to 1.07 feet above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

A long period west swell of 3-4 ft at 14-15 seconds continues to generate breaking waves of 3-5 feet, with local sets up to 6 feet on exposed west-facing beaches today. The period increases to 16-17 seconds Saturday, increasing breaking waves to 4-7 ft with sets up to 8 feet on exposed west-facing beaches and near piers for Saturday, highest in the morning and early afternoon.

The combination tides above 7 feet and elevated surf will result in moderate coastal flooding during the this morning high tide, with minor to locally moderate coastal flooding on Saturday morning. A Coastal Flood Warning remains in effect through early this afternoon, with a Beach Hazards Statement in effect early this afternoon into Saturday afternoon.

nwsAlerts.headline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SATURDAY AFTERNOON... ...COASTAL FLOOD WARNING WILL EXPIRE AT 1 PM PST THIS AFTERNOON
nwsAlerts.description:
* WHAT...Breaking surf of 4 to 7 feet with sets up to 8 feet on exposed west-facing beaches and minor to locally moderate coastal flooding.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and beach erosion. Large breaking waves can cause injury and wash people off beaches and rocks. Low-lying parking lots and boardwalks will flood during morning high tides.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides Saturday morning will be 7.0 to 7.1 feet and occur just after 11 AM PST.
nwsAlerts.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions. Stay off of rock jetties and sea walls. Waves can suddenly and quickly move much farther up the beach than expected; stay back from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.
nwsAlerts.area: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
